description:
The short version of why such simple things (that encourage procrastination) will help you break procrastination forever is this:

Forcing yourself to be more productive isn’t changing who you ARE,

And if the obstacle to your productivity is an internal belief 

(which I find it always is),

FORCE won’t change that, only changing the BELIEF will

The questions I’ve given you are questions I give to clients that help them change their beliefs gradually over time:

FROM: There’s something wrong with me that I can’t do anything about

TO: There’s an obvious pain problem that I can do something about

—

FROM: Only distracting myself helps me feel okay

TO: I LIKE using productivity to make things feel more okay

—

FROM: When something goes wrong everything falls apart.

TO: If I understand what went wrong, I can make things work better next time.

And the other rules, beyond the questions, create space to explore these underlying pains--

They make it feel accessible to slow down and gather insights into the root problem, 

By reducing the intense feeling of pain and threat that the task poses--

because how can you ever gather insights if you numb yourself with scrolling (or something else) before you get a change to look at whats actually happening under the hood?

And if you want help with this yourself, comment ‘pigeon’ and I’ll get you set up with the newsletter where I go into these things in more detail.
transcript: No one believes me when I say this, because anyone who's seriously struggled with this problem feels like they'll never escape it. But procrastination is relatively easy to solve, so I want to talk you through exactly what I would do if I had to overcome procrastination from scratch again. And I wouldn't try to be more productive, I'd follow these four rules, and you're really going to like rule three. Rule one, every day at the start of the day I'd write down what I most wanted to procrastinate, and what I gained by avoiding that task. Not what negative thing I avoid, but what positive thing I gained. Rule two, if I get triggered during a task or before another task throughout the day, I have to write down what triggered me and why it makes me want to avoid the task. Rule three, if I write those things down about a task and it wouldn't cause extreme stress to procrastinate it, I'm allowed to avoid that task for the rest of the day, no questions asked. Rule four, if procrastinating it would cause extreme extreme stress i have to call a loved one that day to help me make a plan for starting the task that day those are the four rules but if you don't want to take my word for it and you want to know why they would fix your procrastination and change your life i chucked more in the caption and i'm going this way if you want to come
